theory.intro: Tax is worked out on **taxable income**, not on everything you earn. Add up the gross income from every source, subtract the allowable tax deductions, and round the result down to the nearest whole dollar. Most people then pay their tax through **PAYG** (pay as you go): the employer withholds an instalment from each pay and sends it to the ATO, so the net pay that reaches the bank account is the gross pay less that instalment.
facts: $\text{Taxable income}=\text{Gross income}-\text{Allowable tax deductions}$, rounded down to the nearest whole dollar.
Gross income means income from every source: salary or wages, bank interest, share dividends, and rent from a property you own.

An expense is an allowable deduction only if it relates directly to earning the income, you paid for it yourself and were not reimbursed, and you can prove it with a receipt. Union fees, tax agent fees and donations to a registered charity are also deductible.
$\text{PAYG instalment}=\text{Annual tax payable}\div\text{Number of pay periods}$, where a year has $52$ weeks, $26$ fortnights or $12$ months.
$\text{Net income}=\text{Gross income}-\text{Tax payable}$, and for a single pay period $\text{Net pay}=\text{Gross pay}-\text{PAYG instalment}$.
steps: Add all sources of gross income
Round down to the nearest whole dollar

foundation.question_text:
An office administrator has a gross income of $\$74\,500$ for the year and allowable tax deductions of $\$1860$.
Calculate her taxable income, to the nearest dollar.

An IT support officer earned $\$88\,300$ in salary and $\$540$ in bank interest. He claims union fees of $\$720$ and work-related software of $\$385$.
Calculate his taxable income, to the nearest dollar.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Add all sources of gross income**
$\text{Gross income}=88\,300+540$
$=\$88\,840$
2. **Subtract the allowable tax deductions**
$\text{Deductions}=720+385$
$=\$1105$
$\text{Taxable income}=88\,840-1105$
$=\$87\,735$

foundation.question_text:
A payroll clerk has a gross income of $\$61\,248.55$ and allowable tax deductions totalling $\$1432.20$.
Calculate her taxable income, rounded down to the nearest whole dollar.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Taxable income}=61\,248.55-1432.20$
$=59\,816.35$
Rounded down to the nearest whole dollar, the taxable income is $\$59\,816$.

foundation.question_text:
A receptionist paid $\$260$ to attend a work-related first-aid course, and her employer reimbursed her the full $\$260$.
Explain why she cannot claim the $\$260$ as an allowable tax deduction.
foundation.solution_text:
An expense is deductible only if the taxpayer paid for it personally and was not reimbursed.
Her employer paid the $\$260$ back to her, so she is not out of pocket and cannot claim it.

development.question_text:
An IT analyst earned a salary of $\$96\,480$, $\$312.75$ in bank interest and $\$188.40$ in share dividends. He claims union fees of $\$684$, home-office equipment of $\$1255.60$ and a tax agent fee of $\$180$.
Calculate his taxable income, rounded down to the nearest whole dollar.
development.solution_text:
1. **Add all sources of gross income**
$\text{Gross income}=96\,480+312.75+188.40$
$=\$96\,981.15$
2. **Subtract the allowable tax deductions**
$\text{Deductions}=684+1255.60+180$
$=\$2119.60$
$\text{Taxable income}=96\,981.15-2119.60$
$=94\,861.55$
3. **Round down to the nearest whole dollar**
The taxable income is $\$94\,861$.

development.question_text:
A receptionist's gross weekly pay is $\$1145$. She claims a work uniform costing $\$7.50$ per week and union fees of $\$12.40$ per week, and she earned $\$96$ in bank interest for the year.
Calculate her annual taxable income, rounded down to the nearest whole dollar.
development.solution_text:
1. **Add all sources of gross income**
$\text{Gross income}=1145\times52+96$
$=59\,540+96$
$=\$59\,636$
2. **Subtract the allowable tax deductions**
$\text{Deductions}=(7.50+12.40)\times52$
$=19.90\times52$
$=\$1034.80$
$\text{Taxable income}=59\,636-1034.80$
$=58\,601.20$
3. **Round down to the nearest whole dollar**
The taxable income is $\$58\,601$.

development.question_text:
An office manager is paid $\$3268$ per fortnight and received $\$425$ in share dividends for the year. Her allowable tax deductions are $\$960$ in union fees and $\$310$ donated to a registered charity.
Calculate her annual taxable income, to the nearest dollar.
development.solution_text:
1. **Add all sources of gross income**
$\text{Gross income}=3268\times26+425$
$=84\,968+425$
$=\$85\,393$
2. **Subtract the allowable tax deductions**
$\text{Deductions}=960+310$
$=\$1270$
$\text{Taxable income}=85\,393-1270$
$=\$84\,123$

mastery.question_text:
An IT technician's net fortnightly pay is $\$2214.30$, after a PAYG instalment of $\$695.70$ has been withheld. Her allowable tax deductions for the year total $\$2486$.
Calculate her annual taxable income, to the nearest dollar.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Gross fortnightly pay}=2214.30+695.70$
$=\$2910$
1. **Add all sources of gross income**
$\text{Gross income}=2910\times26$
$=\$75\,660$
2. **Subtract the allowable tax deductions**
$\text{Taxable income}=75\,660-2486$
$=\$73\,174$

mastery.question_text:
Two administration officers each have a gross annual income of $\$88\,000$. Ravi's allowable tax deductions total $\$1240$ and his income tax payable is $\$18\,664$. Mia's deductions total $\$4600$ and her income tax payable is $\$17\,572$.
Whose net income for the year is greater, and by how much, to the nearest cent?

A payroll officer's annual tax payable is $\$21\,320$, collected in $26$ fortnightly PAYG instalments. After $10$ instalments of $\$760$ each, her employer recalculates the remaining $16$ instalments so that the year's instalments total exactly her tax payable.
Calculate the new fortnightly instalment, to the nearest cent.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Tax already withheld}=760\times10$
$=\$7600$
$\text{Tax still to withhold}=21\,320-7600$
$=\$13\,720$
$\text{New instalment}=13\,720\div16$
$=\$857.50$
